name: financial-report-layout
display_name: Financial Report Layout — Proforma / Projection Dashboard
description: A print-first (WeasyPrint), letter-landscape proforma/projection dashboard document register for compliance financial reports (proformas, income statements, book valuations). V5 CANONICAL SPEC (2026-07-16, post-Fable design audit): Carlito body font (system-ui is a WeasyPrint no-op), horizontal-rules-only row treatment (no fill on total/subtotal — section-banner is the only filled row), server-rendered line-number gutter (not JS — WeasyPrint does not execute JavaScript, so the prior JS-injected gutter never reached the actual PDF), running header via CSS string-set, and table.layout (never flexbox) for chart-beside-table print layout. Verified across the real Bencal proforma family (SPV1, Management, ShareCapital, Commissions): SPV1 2→1pp, Management 2→1pp, ShareCapital 4→3pp (pie/table overlap fixed), Commissions 15→8pp. Supersedes this same component's own prior V1–V3-grounded vault entry (commits 9c8155c/36295c3/0b71534) — V4/V5 were appended to the source draft 2026-07-16 but never landed in this vault; this recipe closes that gap. A sibling of financial-statement-yearend, not the same register — different page geometry (landscape vs. portrait), density (up to 11 period columns vs. 3), and tone.

variants.name: masthead
variants.description: V3: position:relative .masthead wrapping an h1 + description + .sub line, with the draft/version stamp pinned position:absolute (top:0;right:0) — fixes a V1 bug where a float:right stamp let a long description wrap underneath and bleed into it. V5 extends this into a running header: h1 carries string-set:doctitle content(), a .stamp element carries string-set:draftstamp, and @page renders them via @top-left/@top-right plus counter(page) " / " counter(pages) at @bottom-center — all suppressed on @page :first. The BCSC forward-looking-information footer is structurally mandatory on every document in the family (V5 rule 9).

variants.name: wide-table-alignment
variants.description: table.wide + table-layout:fixed so every wide table in the same aligned group resolves identical column geometry (period columns line up table-to-table down the page) — the whole point of a multi-period statement. Label column width tightened V1 25% → V5 24%. The fixed-layout rule is restated inside @media print because some print engines re-resolve layout at print time. V2 clarification: tables align within their own aligned group, not necessarily across the whole document — a document may hold more than one group.

variants.name: semantic-rows
variants.description: tr.total / tr.subtotal / tr.section-banner as row-level role classes, not inline styles. V5 REPLACES the V1 tinted-fill treatment with horizontal-rules-only: th = 1.5px bottom rule, no fill; tr.subtotal = single 1px top rule, no fill; tr.total = double rule (2px top + 2px bottom), no fill; tr.section-banner is now the ONLY filled row and no longer carries the V1 navy ink / uppercase treatment. font-variant-numeric:tabular-nums lining-nums is mandatory on every cell (Carlito's default figures are proportional and would break column alignment without it). Negative values are formatter-level accounting parentheses, e.g. ($1.54M) — never a CSS rule. Nil is an em-dash, never blank or 0. td.tbd (V3, muted bullet •) marks a figure not yet known — distinct from blank (reads as nil) or a fabricated number. td.note (V5) is the left-aligned, non-tabular prose-column treatment — never right-align a note column.

variants.name: line-number-gutter
variants.description: V5 CORRECTS the component's own prior research.md: the line-number gutter must be SERVER-RENDERED at generation time, not JS-injected. WeasyPrint does not execute JavaScript, so the V1–V3 JS injector never reached the actual compliance PDF — the primary render target was silently missing its own line-number column. Emit td.lnum (or th.lnum on header rows) at generation time via a doc-wide running counter prepended to every table row in document order, skipping table.layout rows (class="nolnum"). Width tightened V1 32px → V5 26px, with a right divider.

variants.name: section-block-pagination
variants.description: section.block wraps each heading+note+table+footnote group with break-inside:avoid (V5) so it paginates as a unit — kills orphans. V3 exception: tag the single TALLEST statement in a document .tall so its table may flow across a page break at row boundaries instead of forcing an already-atomic section onto its own page and stranding white space above it (measured: 4 half-empty landscape pages → 3 full pages, no gaps). V3 also resolves the repeating-header open question: author real <thead>/<tbody>, add thead{display:table-header-group} in print so the period header reprints on every page a table spans. V4 hard rule: never use a forced page-break on a SMALL section — it stranded a 10-row table on ~25% of an otherwise-empty page. Prefer break-inside:avoid + break-after:avoid to pack pages top-to-bottom; reserve forced breaks for statements that must not share a page at all.

variants.name: chart-beside-table
variants.description: V5/V4 hard finding: flexbox is BANNED for print in this component family — WeasyPrint overlaps nested flex containers (confirmed: a chart-and-table flex layout overlapped a pie chart onto its adjacent data table). table.layout (a single-row CSS table, its cells zeroing the family's global th/td styling) is the sanctioned mechanism for chart-beside-table and any two-up narrow-table band. .swatch (9px×9px inline-block with a 1px border) marks chart-legend color keys inline in the data-table's own label cells.

aria: Per the draft's own ARIA/accessibility notes: scope="col" on column headers, scope="row" on td.lbl cells. tr.total/tr.subtotal/tr.section-banner each still carry a non-colour signal under V5 (border weight, font-weight) — note this is narrower than this recipe's prior claim: V5 drops the uppercase text-transform and navy ink section-banner previously relied on, so section-banner's non-colour signal is now fill + font-weight + left-align only, not fill + uppercase + colour. td.lnum / th.lnum are decorative (aria-hidden) regardless of render mechanism — unchanged by the V5 JS→server-render correction.

wcag.note: V5 removed the tinted fills that the vault's live token bundle (row-total-bg #eef2f7, row-subtotal-bg #f5f7fa) still encodes as current — total/subtotal now carry zero background colour, distinguished purely by rule weight (single vs. double) and font-weight. This is a STRONGER non-colour-only guarantee than this recipe's prior WCAG note described, not a weaker one — there is no tint left to describe on those two rows.

motion: Print-first static document (also renders on-screen, where the line-number gutter now appears identically to the print output since V5 makes it server-rendered rather than a screen-only JS feature) — no interactive states.
open_questions: oq-1 (carried forward, unresolved): should td.lnum/th.lnum be semantically addressable (e.g. an id per line) so a reviewer's "line 42" can deep-link, or does it remain purely decorative? Not addressed by any of V2–V5.

oq-2 (deferred to project-design's build, per V5's own list, verbatim): full section.block wrapping of every heading+table+note group is applied in the audited Bencal renders but not yet completed as a general rule across all document instances.
oq-3 (deferred to project-design's build): td.note classing of prose "Note" columns — applied on the audited docs, not yet a completed convention.

oq-4 (deferred to project-design's build): migration of the Commissions document's tr:last-child total-hack to the explicit tr.total/tr.subtotal/tr.section-banner semantic classes — currently kept working visually via a restyled fallback; semantic classes are the sanctioned path, not yet applied there.

oq-5 (deferred to project-design's build): a formal .stamp element for the engine-rendered docs' @top-right draft-stamp — Commissions hardcodes its stamp; engine docs currently show doctitle only, no stamp.
oq-6 (deferred to project-design's build): <thead>/<tbody> emission for any table that may span pages — correct today because none currently do; becomes load-bearing the moment one does.

oq-7 (governance gap, flagged not silently fixed): this recipe supersedes the same component's own prior vault entry, which was built from only V1–V3 of the source draft (commits 9c8155c/36295c3/0b71534; no V4/V5 commit exists). The LIVE registered tokens in dtcg-vault/paper/primitive.json and semantic.json, and the document-families table in dtcg-vault/paper/paper.md, still encode the superseded V1 values — 2cm/1.5cm symmetric page margins (V5 uses four distinct asymmetric values, which the current page-margin-inline/page-margin-block token SHAPE cannot represent, not just wrong values), system-ui font, and tinted row-total-bg/row-subtotal-bg fills that V5 removes entirely. Reconciling those values is a DESIGN-TOKEN-CHANGE (requires master_cosign) — out of scope for this DESIGN-COMPONENT pass.

oq-8 (font correction, operational dependency): Carlito (Calibri-metric) replaces system-ui as of V5 — system-ui silently falls back to DejaVu Sans under WeasyPrint. Any render host consuming this recipe needs the fonts-crosextra-carlito package installed (done on the Foundry workspace VM 2026-07-16 per the draft; not verified for any other render host).

oq-9 (drift discipline, per V4 rule D): the engine HEAD (project-proforma's tool-proforma-engine/src/report/bencal_v1_proforma.rs) and this component's canonical CSS must stay byte-identical on @page and break rules — a divergence there is drift to close, not a variant to document.
